facility_name: ASPIRE PHYSICAL RECOVERY CENTER AT CAHABA RIVER
cms_deficiency_category: Resident Rights Deficiencies
deficiency_text: Based on interviews, Resident Identifier (RI) #264's medical record, "FUNDAMENTALS OF NURSING NINTH EDITION", the facility's "PROTOCOL FOR EMERGENT CARE", the facility policy titled "Cardio Pulmonary Resuscitation (CPR)", and a facility reported incident received by the Alabama State Survey Agency, the facility failed to honor the end-of-life wishes of RI #264, a resident with an Advanced Directive to withhold resuscitative measures in the event of cardiopulmonary cessation and an active physician's order for DNR (Do Not Resuscitate) code status. The DNR order directed staff to not initiate CPR when the resident stopped breathing and/or their heart stopped beating. During the evening shift on 02/05/2023, RI #264 was found unresponsive with no pulse or respirations. Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN) #3 did not check RI #264's code status in accordance with the facility's protocol before she initiated CPR. As a result of initiating CPR and activating emergency medical services (EMS), facility staff performed chest compressions and EMS staff continued chest compressions with LUCAS Devise (a mechanical chest compression device), performed endotracheal intubation, performed decompression of RI #264's right lung, and obtained intravenous (IV) and intraosseous (IO) access during the attempt to resuscitate RI This deficient practice placed RI #264, one of three sampled residents reviewed for advance directives and code status, in immediate jeopardy, as the failure of facility staff to honor a resident's end-of-life wishes was likely to cause serious injury, serious harm, serious impairment, or death. The Immediate Jeopardy (IJ) was related to State Operations Manual, Appendix PP, 483.10 Resident Rights. RI #264 was admitted to the facility on 11/26/2021, with diagnoses of Venous Insufficiency, Hypertensive Heart Disease and Chronic Kidney Disease. RI #264's "Alabama Portable Physician Do Not Attempt Resuscitation Order, No/CPR/Allow Natural Death", signed by RI #264's designated health care proxy on 05/12/2022, documented the resident's end-of-life wishes that facility staff failed to honor. Continued From page 16. HCP observed bruises on RI #264's chest after resuscitation efforts. On 01/10/2024 at 9:52 AM, LPN #3 reported that she responded to RI #264 experiencing difficulty breathing on 02/05/2023 at approximately 7:00 PM. RI #264 had labored breathing and O2 saturation of 74%. LPN #3 did not find documentation of DNR status in the physical chart and assumed RI #264 was a full code. LPN #3 obtained crash cart and initiated CPR. LPN #3 admitted facility policy directed staff to first access E-Chart to determine code status and only resort to physical chart if E-Chart unavailable, but she did not follow this policy. LPN #27 on 01/12/2024 at 1:55 PM stated she did not check code status when responding to RI #264's code on 02/05/2023 because she assumed it had already been done. LPN #5 on 01/10/2024 at 7:21 PM responded to code after it was announced and assumed RI #264 was a full code without verifying code status, despite facility policy requiring verification before initiating code. DON interviewed on 01/11/2023 at 5:20 PM stated potential harm of failing to follow advanced directive could result in death or pain if CPR was administered. Administrator interviewed on 01/11/2024 at 12:30 PM confirmed CPR was performed on RI #264 who was a DNR, that the nurse did not follow policy when checking code status, and that disregarding advanced directives caused resident to experience pain and trauma from resuscitation, intubation, and IV administration. Licensed staff had initiated CPR on RI #264 when RI #264 had an active DNR order. The harm of not following an advanced directive would be loss of dignity and rights for the resident. This deficiency was cited as a result of complaint/report number AL00043289. Resident #264 had a DNR (Do Not Resuscitate) order in place dated 01/01/2023 and a health care proxy document directing that resuscitative measures be withheld in the event of cardiopulmonary cessation. On 02/05/2023 at 10:15 PM, staff found RI #264 unresponsive. The facility reported an incident indicating life-saving measures were provided to RI #264 despite the DNR order in place. The EMS run report dated 02/05/2023 documented that EMS was called at 9:37 PM, arrived at 9:46 PM, and performed CPR, intubation, IV access, Advanced Life Support assessment, endotracheal intubation, 5 doses of epinephrine, sodium bicarbonate, calcium chloride, and 750 ml of normal saline bolus using the AHA ACLS Algorithm. Time of death was called at 22:20 (10:20 PM). The facility's investigation documented that LPN #3 failed to adhere to the established protocol for checking code status. Nursing staff had been trained to check the laptop first for code status, and if unavailable, refer to the hard chart. There was no evidence that LPN #3 followed either of these steps before initiating CPR for RI #264. On 01/10/2024, RI #264's Health Care Proxy and spouse confirmed that RI #264 was a DNR and that CPR should not have been performed.
plan_of_correction_text: Past noncompliance: no plan of correction required. The facility took immediate actions to correct the non-compliance and prevent reoccurrence by: On 02/06/2023 the facility identified that Licensed staff had initiated CPR on RI #264 when RI #264 had an active DNR order and began immediate actions to correct the noncompliance. On 02/05/2023 an investigation was initiated, the event was reported to ADPH on 02/06/2023, two LPNs involved both received one on one education and education of all licensed staff was initiated. Education of licensed nurses was completed on 02/10/2023. On 02/06/2023 mock codes were initiated and continued on 02/10/2023 to include all licensed nurses. On 02/06/2023 a review of all DNRs in the building was completed. On 02/06/2023 an emergency Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement (QAPI) meeting was completed related to Emergency Protocols. Monitoring was established that the facility would continue to monitor DNR codes by providing emergent care protocol training with code drill upon hire, quarterly and as needed.
cms_poc_missing_elements: No clear corrective action tied to ensuring code status is checked in the E-Chart/hard chart before CPR as required by policy
No explicit resident/family-specific remediation for RI #264's rights violation beyond acknowledging the event
Monitoring is broad and not clearly tied to auditing actual code-status verification compliance or follow-up accountability
The plan says 'no plan of correction required,' which undercuts the corrective narrative
cms_poc_covered_elements: Immediate resident-specific response: identified the DNR error for RI #264 and initiated investigation/reporting
Staff education: one-on-one education for involved LPNs and education for all licensed nurses
Systemic prevention: mock codes, review of all DNRs, and QAPI/emergency protocol meeting
Ongoing monitoring: emergent care protocol training with code drills upon hire, quarterly, and as needed
cms_poc_reason: The plan addresses the central event with education, mock codes, DNR review, and QAPI follow-up, so it is not boilerplate-only. However, it does not clearly state the key process fix for the cited deficiency: ensuring staff verify code status in the E-Chart and, if unavailable, the hard chart before initiating CPR. The monitoring described is generic and does not specify audits or accountability for compliance with the code-status verification protocol. Because the material process failure is only partially addressed, the plan is partial rather than adequate.
cms_poc_optimizer_feedback: Add a concrete process change requiring staff to verify code status in the E-Chart first and hard chart second before any resuscitation attempt, with documentation expectations. Include targeted audits of code-status verification during mock codes and real events, responsible staff, frequency, thresholds for retraining, and a brief resident/family remediation statement if applicable.

cms_deficiency_category: Resident Rights Deficiencies
deficiency_text: Based on observation, interview, and record review, the facility failed to inform a resident and/or their representative of risks and benefits before installation/use of a transfer pole for 1 of 2 residents (Resident 27), reviewed for accidents. This failure placed the resident at risk for not being fully informed before making decisions regarding their health care, alternative treatment options, and the right to refuse care. Resident 27 admitted to the facility on 2018. Review of the annual Minimum Data Set (an assessment tool) dated 02/22/2024, showed Resident 27 was independent for "lying to sitting" and for "sit to stand." Review of Resident 27's activities of daily living care plan printed on 05/14/2024, showed an intervention for "safety devices," which included use of a transfer pole. Review of Resident 27's electronic health record showed no documentation that Resident 27 had been provided risks and benefits for their use of a transfer pole. Observation and interview on 05/14/2024 at 10:05 AM, showed Resident 27 had a transfer pole next to the left side of their bed. The pole ran from the floor and was secured to the ceiling wall. Resident 27 stated they used the transfer pole every day to "lift up and move around." On 05/17/2024 at 9:41 PM, Staff Q, Certified Nursing Assistant, stated Resident 27 used the transfer pole to help them move in bed and for transferring out of bed. On 05/17/2024 at 1:26 PM, Staff U, Registered Nurse, stated Resident 27 used the transfer pole to help them "get up." Staff U stated they did not know if there needed to be consent prior to use of a transfer pole. On 05/17/2024 at 1:32 PM, Staff N, Charge Nurse, stated that before a transfer pole was installed in a resident's room, there should be an assessment done by therapy and consent should be obtained from the resident and/or their representative. On 05/20/2024 at 12:58 PM, Staff T, Rehab Manager, stated that prior to a resident using a transfer pole, they should get "verbal" consent from the resident and/or their representative. Staff T stated Resident 27 used the transfer pole to "transfer independently." When asked if there was documentation that Resident 27 was provided risks and benefits of using a transfer pole, Staff T stated, "verbal consent is fine." On 05/20/2024 at 2:44 PM, Staff B, Assistant Director of Nursing, stated that a transfer pole was considered an assistive device and they expected there to be documentation that risks and benefits were provided prior to using one for a resident.
plan_of_correction_text: An informed consent was obtained from the selected resident (27). This process included an assessment for appropriate use of the transfer pole, the reason the device was being assessed, risks, and benefits of using or not using the transfer pole, and an opportunity for them to grant consent or declination. This resident selected by DSHS did not demonstrate any negative effects r/t this practice. An audit has been completed. No residents were identified to have been affected by this practice. Rehabilitation Therapy Department manager or designee have started to assess or reassess the devices currently used by residents to determine appropriateness of their continued use. No residents were identified to have been affected by this practice. Moving forward, residents will be provided with risks and benefits when obtaining informed consents. Staff will be provided an in-service on the following process that includes some changes: On admission, the Nurse Admissions Coordinator will inquire about the use of assistive devices that the resident may need or may need to continue using at the facility. They will obtain an informed consent from the resident or their representative so the device may be used upon arrival. The Nurse Admissions Coordinator will obtain an order for a Rehab evaluation, if applicable. The Rehab Manager or designee will follow-up and assess the device or devices and discuss alternatives, risks, and benefits of using this tool to provide the resident or their representative, an opportunity to grant an informed consent or declination. The resident will be offered a written copy of the completed assessment and informed consent form that they signed for their reference. The signed document will be scanned on PCC. The Charge Nurse or designee will verify that the use of assistive devices has appropriate assessments and informed consents obtained from the resident or their representative before they utilize the equipment or device. This audit will be added in the Charge Nurse tasks checklist and verify the presence of an assessment and informed consent. If not, the Charge Nurse or designee will submit a PSA and send out a Clinical Change/Concern (SBAR) for the Rehab Departments follow-up. When there's an urgent need for the device, procedures outlined will be followed.
cms_poc_missing_elements: No explicit retrospective correction for the cited lack of documentation before use
Monitoring frequency/duration and responsible follow-up are vague
Does not clearly address how existing residents with transfer poles will be systematically re-consented if documentation is absent
Urgent-use pathway is mentioned but not operationally detailed
cms_poc_covered_elements: Resident 27 informed consent obtained for transfer pole
Assessment of appropriateness, risks, benefits, and alternatives described
Facility-wide process change for admission and ongoing device review
Staff education/in-service and charge nurse verification/audit process
Documentation/scanning of signed consent form
cms_poc_reason: The plan addresses the core deficiency by stating that informed consent will be obtained, including risks/benefits and alternatives, and it adds a systemic process for admission screening, rehab review, staff education, and charge-nurse verification. However, it is only partially adequate because it does not clearly show a concrete retrospective fix for residents already using transfer poles without documented consent, and the monitoring/audit mechanism lacks specific frequency, duration, and accountability. The cited resident-specific issue is acknowledged, but the plan does not fully demonstrate how the facility will control the existing population at risk or ensure sustained compliance.
cms_poc_optimizer_feedback: To strengthen adequacy, specify a time-bound audit of all current residents using assistive devices/transfer poles, re-consent any resident lacking documentation, define audit frequency and duration (e.g., weekly x 4 weeks then monthly x 3 months), name the responsible role for follow-up, and clarify the urgent-use workflow and documentation requirements.
deficiency_corrected: Deficient, Provider has date of correction

cms_deficiency_category: Freedom from Abuse, Neglect, and Exploitation Deficiencies
deficiency_text: Based on resident council minutes review, interview, and policy review, the provider failed to ensure one of one certified nursing assistant (CNA)/activity staff (Q) who documented allegations of neglect regarding residents' personal care reported by residents, during an 11/12/25 resident council meeting reported those allegation to the administrator according to the provider's policy which resulted in those allegations not being reported to the South Dakota Department of Health (SD DOH) in the required time frame of no more than 24 hours after the allegations were made. CNA/activity staff Q coordinated, attended, and wrote the minutes for the 11/12/25 resident council meeting. She had recorded allegations of neglect made by residents including: residents that can't comb their own hair and wash their own faces are sometimes messy at meals and activity time; some resident(s) have their legs or stomachs showing when they come into the dinning room for meal(s) and for activities; some residents are concerned with how staff sometimes seem too busy and sound upset when answering call lights; and residents brought up nursing cares being done during activity time or in front of other residents, wanting vital signs done in private. CNA/activity staff Q had not reported those allegations to her supervisor or the administrator. Administrator A was notified of the allegations on 11/17/25, which was 5 days after the allegations were made. Social service/activity supervisor E reported those allegations to the SD DOH on 11/18/25.
plan_of_correction_text: Criteria 1: The allegation of neglect was reported to the survey team during the survey as instructed by the Survey Agency office on 11/17/2025. Criteria 2: Interviews were conducted with the resident council and all interview able residents by the Activity staff, Director of Social Services, and Activity Coordinator, as completed on 11/17/25 and 11/21/2025, to determine if there were any unreported allegations of neglect. There were no allegations voiced by the residents. Criteria 3: All facility staff have received in service education on the facility Abuse/Neglect policy and regulatory requirements as completed on 12/22/25 by Administrator. This training included but was not limited to the: need to report all allegations of abuse/neglect to the staff supervisor and/or Administrator immediately. Criteria 4: The QAPI audit tool for the monitoring of compliance with the facility abuse/neglect policy and regulatory requirements will be utilized monthly X 2 months and then quarterly thereafter under direction of the Administrator. Results of these QAPI audits will be reviewed in facility QAPI meetings quarterly.
cms_poc_missing_elements: No clear corrective action addressing the specific failure of CNA/activity staff Q to report the 11/12/25 allegations to the administrator within 24 hours
No resident-specific/systemic process change ensuring allegations from resident council meetings are immediately escalated and reported to SD DOH within required timeframe
No concrete completion/assignment details for who will verify timely reporting of future allegations
cms_poc_covered_elements: Staff education on abuse/neglect reporting requirements
QAPI/audit monitoring plan with monthly then quarterly review
Resident interviews to check for additional unreported allegations
cms_poc_reason: The plan addresses training and ongoing monitoring, and it includes a resident interview sweep for additional concerns. However, it does not directly correct the central cited breakdown: CNA/activity staff Q failed to report the resident council allegations to the administrator within 24 hours, causing delayed state reporting. The plan lacks a specific process for immediate escalation of allegations arising in resident council meetings, and it does not clearly assign responsibility or a time-bound mechanism to ensure future allegations are reported on time.
cms_poc_optimizer_feedback: Add a direct corrective action for the involved staff member and a specific workflow for resident council allegations: immediate notification chain, same-day documentation, 24-hour reporting checkpoint, named responsible person, and audit of council minutes/reporting timeliness for a defined period.

cms_deficiency_category: Nutrition and Dietary Deficiencies
deficiency_text: Based on observation, interview, review of facility policy, and review of the Kentucky Food Guide 2013 Food Code guidance, the facility failed to provide food at a palatable temperature for two (2) residents (Resident #1 and Resident #52). In addition, the facility failed to ensure point of service temperatures (temps) were within acceptable levels. Observation of the 400 Hall lunch meal on 04/02/2024 revealed the hot foods were below the acceptable levels for the point of service temps. The cold food/beverages were above the acceptable levels for the point of service temps. Review of the Kentucky Food Guide 2013 Food Code guidance revealed hot foods should be 135 degrees Fahrenheit (F) or greater and cold food/beverage products should be 41 F degrees or less. Observation during tray line on 04/03/2024 at 11:50 AM revealed temperature reading obtained by the cook were as follows: salisbury steak at 165 degrees F; green beans at 168 degrees F; and macaroni and tomatoes at 155 degrees F. Observation of a lunch meal test tray on 04/03/2024 at 12:53 PM revealed the temperature readings taken by dietary staff were as follows: salisbury steak entree at 118.3 degrees F; hot coffee at 102.9 degrees F; iced tea at 62.1 degrees F; pineapple at 63.1 degrees; green beans at 110.6 degrees F; and macaroni and tomatoes at 116.2 degrees F. Observation revealed the test tray was placed on the food cart at 12:41 PM to be transported to the 400 Hall. During an interview with the DON on 04/05/2024 at 7:30 PM, she stated if a resident complained of cold food on their meal tray, she would make sure it was warmed up. The DON stated she had not received any complaints about cold food from residents; however, she had only worked at the facility for six (6) weeks. During an interview with the Administrator on 04/05/2024 at 8:16 PM, she stated she had not been made aware of any resident complaints related to food not being at the appropriative temperatures. She stated she expected dietary to continue to test trays to ensure the temperatures were appropriate. The Administrator stated depending on how long food was kept at the wrong temperature, bacteria could build up and a resident could contract a food-borne illness. Continued From page 33. During an interview with SRNA #3 on 04/05/2024 at 4:13 PM, she stated residents had complained before about food being cold during all meal times. SRNA #3 stated she would take the meal tray to the employee break room and warm it up in the microwave. She stated she had notified kitchen staff; however, it did not do any good and the kitchen did not offer to prepare another tray for the residents. SRNA #3 stated residents could get sick if they ate cold food. She further stated administration staff did not help with passing hall trays. SRNA #3 stated if the administration staff would assist with passing trays, she thought the resident's may get their food in a more timely manner and it may not be cold. During an interview with SRNA #10 on 04/05/2024 at 4:31 PM, he stated residents did sometimes complain of the food on their meal trays being cold. He stated he took the tray to the microwave and warmed it up. During an interview with LPN #1 on 04/05/2024 at 5:39 PM, she stated residents had complained of food being cold and she re-heated their food in the microwave. She further stated the kitchen was "well aware" of the issue. During an interview with LPN #7 on 04/05/2024 at 5:56 PM, she stated when residents complained of their food being cold, she warmed food up for them or offered to get them a new meal tray. She stated if food was not served at the correct temperature, it could make the resident have stomach issues, diarrhea, or even food poisoning. LPN #7 further stated she made the kitchen aware of the cold food and had them fix a new tray. Continued From page 34. During an interview with the Dietary Manager on 04/05/2024 at 4:59 PM, she stated some residents had voiced concerns about food being cold. The Dietary Manager stated she had noticed some of the hall cart doors were not being closed between tray removal and she had provided education to staff to ensure they were closing the doors. The Dietary Manager stated if a resident complained about cold food, the kitchen staff should warm their tray, prepare a new tray, or fix the resident something else. The Dietary Manager stated if a resident ate something in the "danger zone" temperature range, they could become really sick or get food poisoning. In an interview with the Dietary Manager on 04/05/2024 at 4:59 PM, she stated she had talked to the DON about reminding staff to serve residents their meals as soon as possible when the meal carts arrived on the units. She stated she had educated dietary and nursing staff on keeping the meal cart doors closed and not to let the trays sit on the cart for extended periods of time before they were served. She further stated a resident could contract food poisoning if they ate cold food especially if the temperatures were in the "danger zone." During an interview with the Assistant Director of Nursing (ADON) on 04/05/2024 at 6:36 PM, she stated she was not aware of any complaints about residents receiving cold food. The ADON stated she expected residents to only be served cold food if it was supposed to be cold and for residents to receive their trays timely and their food to be hot.
plan_of_correction_text: On 4/23/24, the Dietary Manager (DM) offered Resident #1 a new tray of food. Resident #1 voiced satisfaction with food offered. Resident #52 no longer in building. All residents have the potential to be affected. On 4/09/24 the DM tested all trays for temperatures at the point of service. Any areas identified as a concern were corrected upon discovery. On 4/23/24, the DM, Director of Nursing (DON), Assistant Director of Nursing (ADON), Environmental Director (EVS), Admission Director (AD), Central Supply, Wound Care Nurse (WCN), Business Office Manager (BOM), and/or Human Resource Manager (HR) audited 100% of all residents with a Brief Interview for Mental Status (BIMS) score of 8 and above for satisfaction of the meal offered. Any areas identified as a concern were corrected upon discovery. Starting on 4/25/24, all staff were re-educated, by DON, LN, Staff Development (SDC), WCN, Assistant Director of Nursing (ADON), Administrator (ADM), Dietary Manager (DM), and Regional Nurse Consultant (RNC) on food temperatures at point of service, resident food preferences and actions to take for substitutions if requested by a resident. A post-test with a passing grade of 100% is required. Staff, including Agency, not available during this time frame will be provided with re-education including post-test by the DON, LN, WCN, ADON, SDC, DM, and/or RNC upon day of return to work. New hires and agency staff will be provided the education and a posttest during orientation by the DON, LN, WCN, ADON, SDC, ADM, and/or RNC. Starting on 4/27/24, the DON, WCN, ADON, SDC, MDS, ADM, DM and/or RNC will complete an audit on 1 test tray.

cms_deficiency_category: Resident Rights Deficiencies
deficiency_text: On 01/01/25, a nursing assistant (NA #1) was asked by RN #1 to go take vital signs on a resident (R) who had already passed away. This was done as a 'friendly joke' or 'teaching opportunity.' NA #1 became distressed by the incident. The resident's family member was upset about what happened, describing it as 'disgusting' and stating the deceased resident 'would have been horrified' that a staff member was sent into the room after the resident had passed away to check vitals as a prank. Based on record review and interview, the facility failed to ensure residents had a right to a dignified existence and were treated with respect and dignity for 1 (R) of 3 (R #1, R and R #17) residents when facility staff used R (without consent) to play a prank/joke on another staff member after R This findings Record review the admission record revealed R was initially admitted on. Record review of Physician Orders revealed that R was full code. Record review of R progress notes dated revealed: (1) '2205 (10:05 pm) resident assessed during hourly rounds. Semifowler (position of laying in bed on back with head and torso raised between 30-45 degrees) in bed, room in good order no issues whatsoever resident Assess results Visible respiration. Code blue initiated. Code blue called out, crash cart obtained, 911 call for assistance from emergency response teams. CPR (cardiopulmonary resuscitation) protocol breaths and chest compression provided 2208 (10:08 pm). 2211(10:11 pm) patient assessment resulting in no detectable heart beat, respirations, CPR resumption at which time ems entered room and immediately deployed team in time post mortem care was rendered/continuing care. At this time care center employees and this nurse removed ourselves from that role.' (2) Progress note identified notification to next of kin and indicated that would need to contact #2 to get funeral information. Per progress note dated at 5:44 am, still waiting on funeral information. The deficient practice was disrespectful and dehumanizing to R and family. On 01/21/25 at 4:36 PM, during an interview, NA #1 said she arrived at work on 01/01/25 at 6:00 AM and at 6:30 AM, RN #1 asked her to go take R vital signs (measurements of the systemic body's essential functions). NA #1 said when she went into R room and usually R would respond to her right away when entering room but this time did not. NA #1 said R dentures did not seem to be sitting right in mouth and R did not respond to her. NA #1 stated she nudged R and noticed R was deceased. NA #1 said she realized R had passed away. NA #1 said she thought R had just passed away, so she left the room to let staff know, and RN #1 was standing outside R room laughing. RN #1 stated that it was a 'cruel rookie joke' that he was playing on her. RN #1 told NA #1 not to say anything because he wanted to play the same 'joke' on another staff. NA #1 said that she was so distraught after the incident that eventually emergency medical services had to be called because she was having a panic attack. On 01/22/25 at 6:57 PM, during an interview, CNA #1 stated R passed away on [date] at 10:56 PM. CNA #1 said RN #1 wanted to play a joke on NA #1 (RN #1 is the night shift manager on the unit). CNA #1 said that when NA #1 got to work on 01/01/25, RN #1 told NA #1 to go take R vital, knowing that R was deceased. CNA #1 confirmed that she did not try to prevent the prank. On 01/22/25 at 7:16 PM, during an interview, NA #2 said that R had passed away and RN #1 wanted to play a joke on staff. NA #2 said when NA #1 got to work around 6:00 am on 01/01/25, RN #1 knowingly directed her to go take vital signs on a deceased resident.
plan_of_correction_text: The facility must develop a plan for ensuring that correction is achieved and sustained. This plan must be implemented, and the corrective action must be evaluated for its effectiveness. The plan of correction is integrated into the quality assurance system. The staff performing post mortem care will complete the Post Mortem Care Audit when a resident expires on their shift. The results of the audit will be reviewed times 4 weeks and then every other week times 2 months, unless there is reported abuse and/or reported infringement of the resident's right to dignity and respect for which immediate action of reporting to Abuse Coordinator who will report to state agency, removing staff member from facility, and ensuring dignity and respect for the resident will occur. This will become a standard of practice as a tool to utilize in the facility. Any report of abuse will be reported to the HCA immediately and an investigation will be started. The Administrator will take any trends to the monthly QAPI meeting for 3 months for further evaluation and/or recommendations. The Administrator will oversee the QAPI process. This Plan of Correction is prepared and submitted as required by law. By submitting this Plan of Correction, Silver City Care Center does not admit that the deficiency listed on this form exists, nor does the Center admit to any statements, findings, facts or conclusions that form the All residents have the potential to be affected by this deficient practice. All residents have the right to live in a home-like environment and not be used as a prank/joke. The Unit Manager audited on 2/25/25 the last 30 days for all residents who had passed in the facility and reviewed the case with staff who performed care and the charge nurse over the resident at the time post mortem care was rendered. Using the Post Mortem Care Audit, each case was reviewed to ensure post mortem care was provided per Genesis Policy, privacy was given, respect and dignity for the resident was maintained until the resident was transported from the facility, and no jokes, no pranks, and no actions taken at the expense of the residents. All staff have been re-educated by Market Operations Advisor and Clinical Resource Nurse on 2/27/25 - 3/3/25. Employees were re-educated on Resident Rights - Dignity & Respect with emphasis on everyone deserves respect and dignity, regardless of their status. Employees also were re-educated on all persons residing in this facility are to be treated with dignity and respect whether living or deceased. Failing to treat a deceased resident with dignity can be considered a form of abuse, even though the individual is no longer living. Mishandling a body or speaking disrespectfully about the deceased violates ethical principles of care. Disrespectful treatment of a deceased resident can cause significant emotional distress to grieving family members. It can also create a negative and demoralizing environment for staff. Market Operations Advisor and Clinical Resource Nurse will educate all nurses on the Post Mortem Care Audit and how and who it is to be completed and it is to be scanned to Market Lead for review and validation. If there are components not completed, the staff member(s) will be suspended immediately pending an investigation.

Tie audits to that workflow with clear frequency, reviewer, and escalation thresholds.

cms_deficiency_category: Resident Assessment and Care Planning Deficiencies
deficiency_text: Resident R62 should have had a resident review PASARR prior to the expiration of the PASARR on 7/20/24. She was only given a short-term approval NF stay by PASARR. The facility is out of PASARR compliance with a resident residing at the facility without a current PASARR on file. R39 was admitted 4/10/23 with anxiety disorder, major depressive disorder, and dementia. Admission PASARR dated 2/23/23 documented Level 1 PASARR, no PASARR Level 2 recommended. On 5/19/23, clinical records documented Aripiprazole (antipsychotic medication) oral tablet 5 mg prescribed for Bipolar/severe anxiety. Subsequent MDS records from 6/24/23 onwards documented bipolar diagnosis. On 1/16/25, review of R39's clinical records lacked evidence that a referral was made to the state mental health authority for an updated PASARR to reflect the new diagnosis of bipolar disorder and the use of aripiprazole (anti-psychotic medication). Based on record review and interview, it was determined that for two (R39, R62) out of two residents reviewed for PASARR, the facility failed to notify the appropriate state-designated authority when the resident's new diagnosis of mental disorder was identified. For R62, the facility failed to request a new PASARR after R62 was diagnosed with visual hallucinations. Additionally, for R39, the facility failed to notify the state-designated authority of a new order for an antipsychotic medication. For R62: 2/4/19 - PASARR documented that patient does not require a Level II PASARR. 12/6/19 - R62 admitted with diagnoses including multiple sclerosis, bipolar disorder and anxiety disorder. 3/28/24 - R62 hospitalized for an infection. 4/5/24 - PASARR documented Level I Outcome: Convalescence Categorical with 60 day convalescent care approval and re-screening requirement. 5/8/24 - care plan updated to include socially inappropriate behavior as evidenced by hallucinations and delusions. 6/6/24 - R62 diagnosed with delusional disorder. 6/13/24 - R62 hospitalized at geropsychiatric hospital for management of delusions/hallucinations. 6/20/24 - R62 re-admitted to facility.
plan_of_correction_text: Due to this being a remote place to track when a new PASARR needed to be completed, moving forward the DON or designee will review all new psych med orders and will forward results to the Social Services Director to have a new PASARR completed. A facility wide sweep was conducted with no other issues identified. The NHA or designee will educate the Social Services director on the new process for obtaining a new PASARR for new psych orders or medication changes. The DON and/or designee will conduct random audits of residents with new psych orders or medications to ensure they do not need a new PASARR. The audit will be performed daily or until 100% compliance is achieved for 3 consecutive days. Random audits will continue once weekly or until 100% compliance is achieved for 3 consecutive weeks. Audits will continue monthly until 100% compliance is achieved for 3 consecutive months. Once 100% compliance is met, the deficient practice will be considered resolved. All audits will be reviewed by the Quality Assurance Committee. Part 1 - Resident R62: A. R62 was not adversely affected by this deficient practice. PASARR for R62 was updated by Social Service Director on 1/30/2025. B. All residents with short-term approved PASSRs have the potential to be affected. C. Root cause analysis determined facility did not have process in place to track when new PASARR needed to be completed. Social Services Director will have tracking tool to determine when new PASARR is required. NHA or Designee will educate Social Services Director on new tracking tool. D. NHA and/or designee will conduct audits of new admissions to ensure new PASARR is not required. Audit will be performed daily or until 100% compliance is achieved for 3 consecutive days. Random audits will continue once weekly or until 100% compliance achieved for 3 consecutive weeks. Audits will continue monthly until 100% compliance achieved for 3 consecutive months. Once 100% compliance met, deficient practice will be considered resolved. All audits reviewed by Quality Assurance Committee. Part 2 - Resident R39: A. R39 was not adversely affected by deficient practice. PASARR for R39 was updated by Social Service Director on 1/30/2025. B. Residents with new diagnosis of mental disorders have potential to be affected by deficient practice. C. Root cause analysis determined facility did not have process in place [continued on next page].

deficiency_text: Based on record review, review of facility policy, and staff interviews, the facility failed to immediately report an incident of verbal abuse for 1 of 1 sampled resident (Resident #8) subjected to name calling and sworn at by a staff member. Failure to report the incident to the state survey agency (SSA) placed Resident #8 and other vulnerable residents at risk of potential and/or continued verbal abuse.
plan_of_correction_text: Immediate action was taken for resident #8 on 11-11-25, resident #8 was removed from the dining room and CNA #2 was reassigned duties following disciplinary action. Director of Nursing reassessed resident #8 on 12-12-25 for lasting effects of any suspected verbal abuse. A thorough investigation was conducted on 12-12-25, interviewing 8 random residents from various households and 3 staff members who were present on 11-11-25. cms_deficiency_category: Quality of Life and Care Deficiencies
deficiency_text: Continued from page 87-88. For Resident 191: A splint was applied to the resident's left arm with a cloth sling that was off and scrunched to the side; their left hand was swollen (almost twice the size of their right hand) and purplish in color. The two rings on the resident's left fingers appeared tight on the knuckles. Resident 191 stated the nurse who applied the splint "put it on too tight." Resident 191 stated their left hand turned "pale, cold, and swollen" throughout the night and was "very painful" and they could not extend their arm out without causing severe pain. They told the nurse on duty in the morning who adjusted/loosened the splint but the swelling had not yet subsided. Staff K (Licensed Nurse) stated a splinted/casted arm was a "high risk condition" because a resident could lose their arm if not assessed or monitored accordingly. There was no indication to monitor Resident 191's left hand for swelling. Staff K stated swelling could happen pretty fast and was dangerous for a splinted/casted arm. There were no indications to elevate Resident 191's left arm to help decrease the swelling; there were no instructions written specifically for the use of the cloth sling; and Resident 191 was not presented with the risk and benefits for wanting to keep their rings on which could further impair circulation and potentially sever the resident's limb. Staff H (Resident Care Manager) stated the baseline care plan was important to be complete, accurate, and identify the needs of newly admitted residents so the nursing staff could provide safe care. The baseline care plan initiated for Resident 191 on admission did not capture the presence of a left arm splint. There was no assessment or monitoring in place to check for Resident 191's skin for pressure points or the resident's left hand/fingers for any changes in color, movement, sensation, or blood return on the nail beds to ensure Resident 191 had adequate blood flowing to their left arm from being splinted. For Resident 60: Review of Resident 60's 02/22/2024 Physician Order summary showed a 12/20/2023 Physician Order for an anticoagulant to be administered to Resident 60 twice daily. This medication was prescribed for Resident 60's irregular heart rhythm. There was no assessment or additional orders to monitor for adverse side effects such as bleeding or bruising. Quality of care is a fundamental principle that applies to all treatment and care provided to facility residents. Based on the comprehensive assessment of a resident, the facility must ensure that residents receive treatment and care in accordance with professional standards of practice, the comprehensive person-centered care plan, and the residents' choices. This REQUIREMENT is not met as evidenced by: Based on observation, interview, and record review, the facility failed to identify and provide care and services in accordance with the resident's goals and professional standards of practice in the areas of splint use and monitoring impacts of blood thinners and sleep medications for 4 of 20 residents (Residents 191, 60, 85, & 44) reviewed for quality of care. Resident 191 experienced harm when their left hand became swollen and self-reported a severe level of pain when the facility failed to implement measures to monitor the resident's circulation and blood flow to their broken left arm after wound treatment and reapplication of the hard splint. These failures placed residents at risk for unmet needs, decline in medical status, and a decreased quality of life. Review of Resident 44's medical record showed an active order for an AC medication to be administered twice daily. There were no indications to assess or monitor for signs and symptoms of active bleeding related to AC medication use. Review of Resident 44's February 2024 MAR showed they had received the AC medication twice daily. During an interview on 02/26/2024 at 10:13 AM, Staff E stated Resident 44 was receiving an AC medication and they were not monitoring for signs of active bleeding, but they should to ensure Resident 44 was not having adverse side effects from the medication and staff would know how to care for her while on a blood thinner medication. Review of the February 2024 POs showed Resident 85 received a medication for sleeping daily. Review of the February 2024 MAR showed no documentation to assess and/or monitor the sleeping hours to determine if the medication was effective or not. In an interview on 02/26/2024 at 1:56 PM, Staff G reviewed Resident 85's record and stated there should be indications to monitor Resident 85's hours of sleep to determine if the medication was helpful, but there was none. cms_deficiency_category: Infection Control Deficiencies
deficiency_text: Based on observation, clinical record review, Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Guidelines, Policy review and staff interviews, the facility failed to prevent the spread of infection for 2 of 2 residents who tested positive for influenza A (Residents #17 and #38). In addition, the facility failed to implement droplet precautions, sanitize the barrier used during a blood sugar check for 1 of 2 residents observed (Resident #23), and failed to adhere to infection control practices during medication administration when dirty gloves contacted oral medication for 3 of 7 resident observed (Residents #16, #19 and #34). On 1/2/26, the facility failed to follow infection control protocols after Resident #17 tested positive for influenza A. After Resident #17 tested positive for influenza A, the facility failed to initiate isolation or droplet precautions to prevent the spread of influenza A. On 1/6/26, Resident #38 (Resident #17's roommate) displayed signs and symptoms of an upper respiratory tract infection with wheezing (a whistling sound indicating difficulty of air moving through the lungs). Resident #38 required the use of prednisone They didn't direct the visitor to perform hand hygiene prior to visiting Resident #17's roommate. Staff G failed to apply goggles or a face shield, remove her face mask before exiting the room and perform hand hygiene immediately upon exiting the room. Staff G placed her hands on the meal cart and moved it down the hallway a few feet, then asked Staff H, Certified Medication Aide (CMA), if she had some hand sanitizer. Staff G sanitized her hands and without sanitizing the meal cart, she touch it in the same place she just had her hands and continued to serve 4 more resident room trays. On 1/6/26 at 11:49 AM Staff H reported they are to wear a mask, gown, gloves, and make sure to wash their hands on way out of the room. She stated Resident #17 tested positive for influenza A. He went to the emergency department (ED) on Friday. She returned to work on Monday (1/5/26). He didn't have PPE outside the room, so she just wore a mask and gloves to go in his room on Monday. On 1/6/26 at 11:51 AM the Director of Nursing (DON) stated she would save everyone a lot of time and work. Resident #17 went Friday (1/2/26) to the ED and returned that same day positive for influenza A. The nurse didn't pass on the information through the report, so no one knew about it on the weekend. On Monday (1/5/26) she put signs on the front and back door of the facility regarding visitation. She just put the CDC Droplet Precaution Sign on Resident #17's room door and started to complete staff education regarding communication and isolation precautions. She printed off the policy for education and got a standing order for Tamiflu for the residents. She said the nurse should have notified the on-call nurse 1/2/26 which would have been her and then she would have alerted the Infection Preventionist. They would instruct to place Resident #17 on droplet precautions. The facility should have placed Resident #17 on precautions on 1/2/26 when he returned from the hospital, but it got missed. They just placed him on droplet precautions at that time. The General Progress Note dated 1/6/26 at 6:18 PM documented a Provider visit for Resident #38 (roommate of Resident #17) with a chief complaint of signs and symptoms of upper respiratory illness (URI) with chills and malaise (extreme tiredness) for 2 days. The Progress Note indicated the staff alerted the nurse that Resident #38 had signs and symptoms of a URI. The hospital diagnosed his roommate with influenza A on Friday (1/2/26). The Progress Note documented Resident #38 as alert and appeared sick with wheezing. The Provider ordered Resident #38 to start Z-pack antibiotics, a prednisone (steroid therapy used to treat swelling) taper, and nebulizer (breathing) treatments as needed. On 1/7/26 at 8:11 AM Staff I, CNA, reported she worked 1/5/25 and they didn't have residents placed on isolation precautions. No one reported Resident #17 had influenza A. Interview completed on 1/7/26 8:16 AM Staff F reported she didn't work the weekend (1/2/26 - 1/3/26). If she would have worked the weekend, she would have put Resident #17 on precautions. Resident #17's roommate was out of the room and all over the facility all weekend and Monday (1/5/16). Resident #17's roommate had symptoms of the flu that morning and he is really sick. He even had a visitor yesterday and they tried to turn away the visitor, but they refused. The visitor at least wore a mask when she visited Resident #17's roommate. Resident #17 should have started precautions right away. During an interview on 1/7/26 at 10:11 AM Staff B, Registered Nurse (RN), reported he worked the weekend of 1/3/26 and 1/4/26. He didn't put any residents on any type of isolation precautions. It was possible that staff could have gone in the room to provide care to Resident #17 without PPE, but he didn't go into Resident #17's room himself. Interviews completed on 1/7/26 at 10:25 AM Staff F and Staff H reported the instruction they received said they only had to wear masks and gloves to enter Resident #17's room. On 1/7/26 at 11:39 AM Staff E, Assistant Director of Nursing (ADON)/Infection Preventionist (IP), reported it happened late at night and it wasn't passed through report that Resident #17 tested positive for influenza A. The nurse should have notified the on-call nurse, passed it through report and placed the resident on isolation precautions. The resident should be kept in their room for 7 days or until no signs and symptoms. She reported being the on-call nurse on 1/2/26 and never received any calls regarding a resident with influenza. She worked on Saturday (1/3/26) and Sunday (1/4/26) night shift and still never received a report of a resident positive for influenza A.
plan_of_correction_text: The facility immediately addressed the infection control concerns identified during the survey. Director of Nursing, Assisted Director of Nursing, Staff F, Staff G, Staff H, were immediately re-educated on proper droplet precautions. All other staff were educated on 1/7/2026. Residents #17 and #38 were immediately placed on droplet-based precautions per facility policy and CDC guidelines. Proper personal protective equipment (PPE) and hand hygiene supplies were made readily available. The Infection Preventionist reviewed the care of affected residents to ensure infection prevention measures were in place and resident safety was maintained. Resident #38 tested negative for the flu on 1/7/2026. Other residents with signs and/or symptoms of the Flu were tested with no further positive results. The facility conducted an audit of residents requiring transmission-based precautions and residents receiving blood glucose monitoring and medication administration to assess compliance with droplet precautions, use of gloves and barriers during blood sugar monitoring, and hand hygiene before, during, and after medication administration. Any identified deficiencies were corrected immediately. The facility implemented systemic changes including review of Infection Prevention and Control Program (IPCP) policies and procedures, reinforcement of CDC and facility-specific infection control guidelines, mandatory in-service education for licensed nursing staff on 1/15/2026, ensured availability and accessibility of PPE and hand hygiene supplies, and enhanced supervision by nursing leadership during medication passes. The DON or designee will complete infection control observations during medication passes and blood sugar monitoring along with any droplet precautions weekly for four weeks, then monthly for three months, and quarterly thereafter. Audit results will be reviewed during QA/QAPI meetings.

Staff re-education on droplet precautions, PPE, and hand hygiene
Systemic review of IPCP policies and CDC/facility guidelines
Audit/observation plan for transmission-based precautions, glucose checks, and medication passes
QA/QAPI review with defined weekly/monthly/quarterly monitoring

It is sufficiently responsive to the material deficiency narrative.

cms_deficiency_category: Resident Assessment and Care Planning Deficiencies
deficiency_text: Based on interview and record review, the facility failed to ensure the Minimum Data Set (MDS -an assessment tool) accurately reflected the status for 2 (Resident 80 & 5) of 19 residents reviewed for accuracy of assessments. This failure placed the residents at risk for unmet care needs and a diminished quality of life. Resident 5: According to a 09/25/2024 Annual MDS Resident 5 had multiple medically complex diagnoses and required the use of psychotropic medications during the assessment period. This MDS showed Resident 5 was not currently considered by the state Level 2 Preadmission Screening and Resident Review (PASRR) process to have a Serious Mental Illness (SMI). Review of a 09/29/2023 Level 1 PASRR showed staff identified Resident 5 had SMI indicators of a mood and anxiety disorder and required a referral for a Level 2 evaluation. Review of a 12/14/2023 PASRR Notice of Determination showed Resident 5 was assessed to have a diagnosis and required specialized behavioral health services. The Level 2 PASRR evaluation was completed on 12/14/2023 with recommendations for Resident 5's specialized plan of care established. In an interview on 03/27/2025 at 9:22 AM, Staff D (MDS Coordinator) stated if Resident 5 had a Level 2 evaluation and was determined to have an SMI, it should be accurately identified on the 09/25/2024 Annual MDS. According to Resident 5's 12/23/2024 Quarterly MDS, staff assessed the resident to have a pressure ulcer/injury, a scar over bony prominence, or a non-removable dressing/device during the assessment period. No pressure ulcers were identified as current on this MDS. Review of nursing progress note from 12/23/2024 at 3:02 PM showed staff documented an assessment that Resident 5's skin was intact with no wounds present and no new skin issues noted. A 12/23/2024 weekly skin audit completed at 4:00 PM showed Resident 5 continued to have previously identified chronic discoloration to both lower legs and fading bruises to the left arm. No pressure ulcers, scars over bony prominences, or non-removable dressing/devices were documented as being present during the assessment.
plan_of_correction_text: Resident #5 had a correction made to 12/23/24 MDS for skin findings and the 09/25/24 MDS will be corrected to reflect a PASRR Level 2. Resident #80 had their J/25 MDS corrected to reflect resident was discharged home in stable condition with their spouse. The MDS Coordinator/Designee will audit MDSs for the last 30 days for accuracy according to Care Plans, Evaluation, and Documentation. Discrepancies found will be immediately corrected. The MDS Coordinators will be educated on the resident Assessment policy. The MDS coordinator will audit MDS, evaluations and care plans weekly x4 weeks, then monthly x2 months, then quarterly to ensure the MDS accurately reflects Care Plans, Evaluations and documentation. Discrepancies found will be immediately corrected and brought to QAPI for further evaluation.

cms_deficiency_category: Quality of Life and Care Deficiencies
deficiency_text: Based on record review, policy review, resident, and staff interviews, the facility failed to have a restorative program available for all residents at the facility. The facility failed to implement a restorative plan for 2 of 2 residents that reported if they had an option to do therapy, they would (Residents #36 and #43). The facility reported a census of 43 residents. Resident #36's Minimum Data Set (MDS) assessment dated 11/12/25 documented a Brief Interview for Mental Status (BIMS) of 15, indicating no cognitive impairment. The MDS listed Resident #36 as dependent on staff (requires 2 staff to complete the task and the staff do all the work) for toileting, dressing, transfers and personal hygiene. The MDS included diagnoses of stroke, anxiety, depression, and hemiplegia (the loss of muscle function, causing an inability to move voluntarily to one entire side of the body, affecting the face, arm, and leg, caused by brain damage to the opposite side of the brain). Resident #36 Care Plan on 1/8/26 documented he is participating in the Restorative Nursing Program and needs strengthening and stretches to prevent contractures and to perform restorative exercises as order. The review of Resident #36's December 2025 Documentation Survey Report (a facility computer generated report from the resident medical record about the residents' activities of daily living, restorative, and activity attendance) on 1/8/26 lacked a restorative program. The review of Resident #36's January 2026 Documentation Survey Report on 1/8/26 lacked a restorative program. In an interview on 1/8/26 at 12:12 PM Resident #36 reported it was nice in the past to attend the restorative program. He added he thought might have participated twice in the past 5 years of living at the facility. He explained he would like to try a restorative program and if he liked it, he would possibly do it every day. Resident #43's MDS assessment dated 9/24/25 identified a BIMS score of 6, indicating severe cognitive impairment. Resident #43 needed moderate assistance (required 1 staff to assist but do less than half the effort) for standing, transfers, and walking up to 50 feet. The MDS included diagnoses of
plan_of_correction_text: Residents #36 and #43 were immediately evaluated by Nursing and Therapy. Physician and therapy referrals were initiated/reviewed as indicated. Resident #43 is still on therapy caseload and will have an individualized restorative nursing program upon completion. An individualized restorative nursing program was implemented to address identified deficits in range of motion, mobility, positioning, and functional decline for resident #36. Care plans were updated to reflect current restorative interventions, frequency, and measurable goals. Nursing staff were re-educated on proper implementation and documentation of restorative programs. A facility-wide audit was conducted on all residents receiving or appropriate for restorative nursing services. Residents were assessed for decline in mobility or ROM, changes in ADLs, and inconsistent or absent restorative documentation. Any resident identified as at risk received immediate evaluation and appropriate restorative interventions and care plan updates. Implemented a standardized restorative tracking tool to ensure daily completion, resident participation, and accurate documentation of refusals and outcomes. Therapy and Nursing now collaborate weekly to identify residents appropriate for restorative programs. Education provided to all nursing staff on purpose and importance of restorative nursing, proper techniques and documentation, and reporting changes in resident condition promptly. The DON or designee will audit restorative programs weekly for four weeks, then monthly for three months, and quarterly thereafter. Audits will include presence of physician orders, accurate and complete documentation, and evidence of resident participation and progress. Audit results will be reviewed during QA/QAPI meetings. Identified issues will result in immediate corrective action and staff re-education as needed.
cms_poc_missing_elements: Does not clearly address the cited failure to have a restorative program available for all residents at the facility
No explicit process to identify and enroll all eligible residents who reported wanting therapy/restorative services
Limited specificity on how residents like #36 and #43 will be offered/started on restorative programming based on their expressed preference and functional status
cms_poc_covered_elements: Immediate evaluation of affected residents #36 and #43
Resident-specific restorative intervention for #36 and planned individualized program for #43
Care plan updates and staff re-education
Facility-wide audit of residents receiving or appropriate for restorative services
Ongoing monitoring/audits with QA/QAPI review
cms_poc_reason: The plan contains meaningful corrective actions: it addresses the two named residents, adds restorative interventions, updates care plans, educates staff, and establishes audits and QA/QAPI follow-up. However, the deficiency narrative is broader than the two residents and cites a facility failure to have a restorative program available for all residents, including residents who stated they would like therapy. The plan does not clearly describe a comprehensive screening/enrollment process for all at-risk residents or explicitly ensure the program is available facility-wide to residents who desire it. That material gap keeps it from being fully adequate.
cms_poc_optimizer_feedback: Add a clear facility-wide restorative screening and referral workflow for all residents, especially those expressing interest in therapy/restorative services or showing functional decline, with responsibility, timing, and documentation steps. Explicitly state how eligible residents will be identified, offered restorative programming, and tracked to ensure the program is available to all appropriate residents, not just the two cited residents.

deficiency_text: Based on record review and interview, the facility failed to ensure care plans were revised in 1 of 2 residents reviewed for care plans. Diagnoses included, but were not limited to, unspecified dementia, unspecified severity, without behavioral disturbance, psychotic disturbance, mood disturbance, and anxiety. The resident need supervision for transfer and mobility with substantial help for mobility. Current physician orders included but were not limited to: Weekly weights every day shift every Sunday for There was a current care for a seborrheic lesion to the right cheek dated 8/8/23. There was a current care plan of nutritional risk for inadequate food/beverage intake with dementia and triggered for 10% weight loss dated 6/17/24. cms_deficiency_category: Freedom from Abuse, Neglect, and Exploitation Deficiencies
deficiency_text: According to an 11/18/2024 Admission MDS, Resident 42 was dependent on staff for bed to chair transfers. The MDS showed Resident 42 had a diagnosis of paralysis. Review of Resident 42's 12/26/2024 High Risk for Falls related to Paralysis Care Plan (CP), staff would anticipate and meet the needs of the resident. Resident 42's care plan showed "had an actual fall with no injury" and neurological checks would be completed for the 05/22/2025 fall. In an observation and interview on 06/09/2025 at 10:23 AM Resident 42 was lying in bed with bilateral above the knee amputations. Resident 42 stated they fell after staff placed them in their wheelchair crooked and they attempted to reposition themselves. Resident 42 stated the wheelchair tipped over backward and they "hit their head so hard on the corner of the wall." Review of the investigation documents showed the incident report for Resident 42 identified they hit their head during a fall on 05/22/2025. The report showed Resident 42 was transferred by two staff with a mechanical lift to their wheelchair and Resident 42 attempted to self-adjust after the staff placed them in their wheelchair causing the wheelchair to tip over backwards with staff still present in the room. The report showed Resident 42 hit their head on the corner of the wall when their wheelchair tipped over backward. The investigation of Resident 42's fall showed "neurological assessment initiated." Review of the 05/22/2025 investigation and Resident 42's records showed no neurological assessment was done. Resident 42's incident report showed there was no predisposing situation factors for the fall including whether the resident was uncomfortable in their wheelchair after the transfer. The investigation did not include statements from the two staff members that transferred Resident 42 investigating if they ensured the residents comfort after placing them in their wheelchair. In an interview on 06/13/2025 at 1:32 PM Staff B (Director of Nursing) stated they did not have documentation of a completed neurological assessment as part of the investigation file or in Resident 42's health records but should. Staff B stated a skin assessment documenting measurements and appearance of Resident 42's skin should have been done but was not. Staff B stated it was important to complete these assessments as part of the investigation to ensure the residents did not have further injuries or other negative health outcomes. Staff B stated they expected staff to complete all sections of the incident report as part of the investigation to include assessment of the environmental factors and predisposing situation factors, but staff did not for Resident 42's falls. According to a 04/25/2025 Quarterly MDS, Resident 3 had multiple medically complex diagnoses, required substantial assistance with transfers, and was dependent on staff for toileting hygiene. In an interview on 06/09/2025 at 10:18 AM, Resident 3's family stated they were concerned about the resident having recent falls. Observations on 06/09/2025 at 12:38 PM, showed Resident 3 lying in bed with their call light in reach. Review of a revised 08/16/2024 risk for falls CP showed Resident 3 had a history of frequent falls and gave directions to staff to anticipate resident needs, ensure the resident's call light was within reach, and keep the room free of clutter due to poor eyesight. Review of a revised 05/18/2024 "actual fall" CP showed an intervention to assist Resident 3 with the bathroom upon awakening, before/after meals, and at bedtime. Review of a 01/05/2025 12:00 PM facility incident report showed Resident 3 was found in their room, lying on the floor face down, with their wheelchair nearby. The investigation was blank under the "Predisposing Environmental Factors" assessment section showing staff did not indicate if Resident 3's room was cluttered, if wheelchair locks were working, or if the resident had what they needed within reach. There was no information included in the report to show if Resident 3 needed assistance with toileting or other care needs and/or when the last time any assistance was provided to the resident prior to the fall. Review of a 01/20/2025 6:30 PM facility incident report showed Resident 3 was found on the floor by their bed with their wheelchair behind them. The investigation was blank under the "Predisposing Environmental Factors" assessment section of the incident report showing staff did not indicate if Resident 3's room was cluttered, if wheelchair locks were working, or if the resident had what they needed within reach. There was no information included in the report to show if Resident 3 needed assistance with toileting or other care needs and/or when the last time any assistance was provided to the resident prior to the fall. According to an 04/16/2025 Significant Change MDS, Resident 26 had multiple medically complex diagnoses including and a history of repeated falls. This MDS showed Resident 26 had a fall with injury since the previous assessment and required substantial assistance with transfers and toileting hygiene. Review of a revised 05/24/2024 fall CP showed Resident 26 had low blood sugars, confusion, poor balance, impulsive behavior, and received high-risk medications. Observations on 06/08/2025 at 12:21 PM showed Resident 26 sitting on their bed with their walker nearby. In an interview at this time, Resident 26 stated they had recent falls. Review of a 01/11/2025 4:04 AM facility incident report showed Resident 26 was found standing staring at the wall, and began lowering themselves to the floor. The staff in the room assisted Resident 26 to their knees. There was no information included in the report to show if staff assessed Resident 26's blood sugar, needed assistance with toileting or other care needs, and/or when the last time any assistance was provided to the resident prior to the fall. Review of a 03/24/2025 12:08 AM facility incident report showed Resident 26 was found on the floor in the hallway with injuries to their face. The investigation records showed Resident 26's call light was on at the time of the fall. There was no information included in the report to indicate how long the resident's light was on or how long it was since they received toileting assistance from staff, prior to the fall. There was no information to show if staff assessed Resident 26's blood sugar after the fall. Review of a 05/01/2025 10:00 PM facility incident report showed Resident 26 was found on the floor by their bed with a broken walker next to them and injuries to their finger. The investigation records showed Resident 26's call light was on at the time of the fall. There was no information included in the report to indicate how long the resident's light was on at the time of the fall or if staff assessed Resident 26's blood sugar after the fall. In a joint interview on 06/13/2025 at 11:34 AM with Staff B and Staff G (Regional Director of Clinical Operations), Staff G stated it was important to try and figure out the root cause of a fall so staff would know how to formulate the interventions to prevent further falls and decrease the risk for injuries. Staff B stated the incident reports for Residents 3 and 26 were not thorough and should have, but did not include more information and assessments. Refer to F689 - Free of Accidents Hazards. Based on observation, interview, and record review, the facility failed to ensure thorough and complete investigations for 4 of 7 residents (Resident 28, 42, 3, & 26) reviewed for falls. Failure to conduct a thorough investigation placed residents at risk for further injuries, potential abuse/neglect, and other negative health outcomes. According to a facility policy titled, "Freedom from Abuse, Neglect, Corporal Punishment, Involuntary Seclusion, Mistreatment, Misappropriation of Resident Property, and Exploitation," dated March 2025 According to facility policy titled 'Abuse Investigation,' dated October 2022, and 'Resident Falls Management,' dated November 2016, the facility would assess and decrease clutter in the room, assess footwear and guarantee the resident's footwear fit appropriately, and evaluate lighting in the room and adjust as needed. According to a 05/28/2025 Admission Minimum Data Set (MDS) Resident 28 admitted to the facility on /2025 with no memory impairment. The MDS showed Resident 28 had a history of falls. In an observation and interview on 06/09/2025 at 9:28 AM, Resident 28 was lying in bed with a bandage to their left knee and elbow. Resident 28 stated they had a fall the other day causing an abrasion to their left knee and elbow. Review of a 05/24/2025 investigation for a fall showed the nurse answered Resident 28's call light and found the resident sitting on their bed and reported they fell, with skin injuries to their left knee and elbow. The incident report showed a 'Neurological Assessment' was initiated with no documentation of the assessment being done. The investigation was blank under the 'Predisposing Environmental Factors' assessment section of the incident report showing the environment was not assessed for causative factors such as clutter, wet floor, or appropriate footwear for Resident 28's fall on 05/24/2025. The investigation did not include a skin assessment of the left knee skin. An example of neglect was failure to implement and monitor care planned interventions.
plan_of_correction_text: A. How the nursing home will correct the deficiency as it relates to the residents: 1. Resident #28 fall on 5/24/25 investigation reopened for review and ensure thorough investigation to update care plan preventing repeat falls. Skin assessment on L knee and elbow completed and already healed. No negative outcome noted to resident with the deficiency. 2. Resident #42 fall on 5/22/25 investigation re-opened for review and ensure thorough investigation to update care plan preventing repeat falls. No negative outcome was noted to resident with the deficiency. 3. Resident #3 falls on 1/05/2025, 1/20/25 investigation re-opened for review and ensure thorough investigation to update care plan preventing repeat falls. There was no negative outcome noted to residents related to falls. 4. Resident #26 fell on 1/11/25, 3/24/25, 5/01/25 were re-opened, for review and ensure thorough investigation to update care plan preventing repeat falls. No negative outcome was noted to resident with the deficiency. 5. Nursing staff were educated on documentation of predisposing environmental conditions, check blood sugar during falls, completing neuro sheets and record keeping, completing statements when was the resident last seen or toileted, how long the call light is on, wheelchair observation that could contribute to the fall to rule out abuse and neglect and update individualized care plan on preventing repeat falls. 6. DNS and ED were educated on incident thorough investigations, root cause analysis to rule out abuse and neglect and ensure safety of the residents. B. How the nursing home will act to protect residents in similar situations: 1. Facility reviewed falls in the last 30 days 1. Ensure fall care plan intervention is placed in accordance with the root cause of individual resident fall. No other resident noted to have negative outcome with the deficiency. 2. Re-education provided to ED and DNS on risk management, completion of investigation to rule out abuse and neglect, identify root causes (5 why's) and ensure develop care plan intervention for fall. 3. Nursing staff were educated on documentation of predisposing environmental conditions, check blood sugar during falls, completing neuro sheets and record keeping, completing statements when was the resident last seen or toileted, how long the call light is on, wheelchair observation that could contribute to the fall to rule out abuse and neglect and update individualized care plan on preventing repeat falls. 4. IDT clinical meeting will review fall incidents investigation, progress notes resident's notes to identify the root cause to rule out abuse and neglect, develop intervention and update the individualized care plan for fall preventions. 5. DNS or designee will audit resident falls to ensure thorough investigation as where identify root cause of the fall, ensure documentation of predisposing environmental factors, documentation of vital sign including blood sugar checks, completion of neuro sheets and record keeping per protocol, and update the individualized care plans to prevent resident's repeat fall. 6. DNS or designee will audit falls incidents weekly x 1 month, bi-weekly x 1 month, then monthly. All audit results will be presented to QAPI for review and developed intervention as needed. Audit will continue until QAPI IDT determines facility in substantial compliance.
cms_poc_missing_elements: Does not clearly address the specific missing neurological assessment and skin assessment for Resident 42 beyond general education
Does not specifically address the blank/insufficient predisposing environmental factor documentation for Resident 3 and similar cases in a concrete resident-specific way
No clear corrective action for Resident 26's cited fall narrative is visible because the narrative is truncated and the plan remains generic
Monitoring lacks a precise sample size/criteria and does not specify how compliance will be verified for each cited documentation element
cms_poc_covered_elements: Reopened investigations for the cited residents/falls
Staff education on fall investigation documentation, neuro checks, blood sugar checks, environmental factors, toileting/last seen, and wheelchair observations
Leadership education for DNS/ED on root cause analysis and incident review
Ongoing audit schedule for fall incidents with QAPI review
cms_poc_reason: The plan contains meaningful corrective actions: it reopens the cited fall investigations, provides staff and leadership education, and establishes audits/QAPI follow-up. However, it is only partially responsive to the deficiency narrative because the central cited failures were incomplete fall investigations and missing assessments/documentation (especially Resident 42's missing neuro and skin assessments and Resident 3's blank environmental/predisposing-factor sections). The plan mostly states generic retraining and auditing without clearly showing that the specific missing assessments/documentation will be completed or how compliance with those exact elements will be verified for the cited residents and similar cases.
cms_poc_optimizer_feedback: Tie the correction directly to each cited failure: specify completion of the missing neuro/skin assessments for Resident 42 if still clinically relevant, completion of the omitted environmental/predisposing-factor documentation for Resident 3, and a concrete checklist for all fall investigations. Add measurable audit criteria (e.g., 100% of fall reports reviewed for required fields) and a defined escalation process for noncompliance.

cms_deficiency_category: Nutrition and Dietary Deficiencies
deficiency_text: This REQUIREMENT is not met as evidenced Based on observation and interview, it was determined that the facility failed to ensure food was stored and served in a manner that prevents food borne illness to the residents. Findings include: 1. 1/13/25 6:03 AM - An observation in the dry storage room revealed several food item bags that were opened but not dated. There were three bags of bread and a bag of cake mix powder. The findings were confirmed with E25 (Assistant Food Service Director) on site. 2. 1/13/25 6:11 AM - An observation in the walk-in freezer revealed some food debris on the floor. An opened bag of shrimp did not have a date. The findings were confirmed with E25 on site. 3. 1/13/25 9:15 AM - An observation in the walk-in refrigerator revealed a dated half bag of poultry meat stored together with two bags of un-opened same type of poultry meat without dates. The surveyors were not certain whether they belonged to the same batch. There were also a bottle of apple juice and a grape jelly undated, and a discolored vegetable salad dated 1/3/25 which was removed by E25 upon noticed. 4. 1/14/25 2:17 PM - A review of the three-month food temperature log from October to December, 2024 revealed that the temperature of 22 out of 279 (7.9%) meals were not recorded in the log. Staff failed to follow protocols for proper food storage, dating and labeling. All unlabeled or undated food in the walk-in refrigerator was labeled or discarded by the Food Service Director. The cook failed to follow the protocols for logging the food temperatures at mealtimes.

deficiency_text: Continued from page 25. Based on the South Dakota Department of Health (SD DOH) complaint report review, interview, document review, record review, and policy review, the provider failed to ensure two of two sampled residents with expressed feelings of emotional distress (57 and 78) allegations of sexual abuse reported to social services designee (F) regarding having been touched in their private areas without the residents' consent by one of one certified nursing assistant (CNA) (D) and an unidentified staff member were thoroughly investigated. The provider was to protect residents from physical and psychosocial harm during the investigation, assess the resident for injury, notify the physician, and suspend the accused employee during the investigation.
